To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) chronic renal failure (5/6 nephrecomy) results in a downregulation of Na+/K+ - ATPase activity and protein expression, which is not observed in rats subjected to supranal aortic bandings and 2) 5/6 nephecomy rats have a prolonged calcium recovery time constant in their isolated myocytes, which is associated with decreases in SERCA2a activity, protein expression and mRNA.
rats subjected to 4 wk of 5/6 renal ablation develop cardiac hypertrophy, impaired contractile function, and altered calcium cycling that is not accounted for by hypertension alone.
5/6 renal ablation in rats produces cardiac hypertrophy with altered contractile function and calcium handling.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of chronic renal failure and the development of hypertension on cardiac gene expression, calcium cycling, contractile function, and cardiac hypertrophy.
the effects of chronic renal failure and its attendant hypertension on cardiac function and gene expression.
understanding the molecular mechanisms of the development of cardiac hypertrophy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the observed alterations in calcium cycling and contractility are a consequence of the observed changes in cardiac gene expression.
chronic renal failure leads not only to alterations in cardiac calcium homeostasis but also to changes in cardiac gene expression.
the observed changes in the heart are due to a complex interaction of multiple factors including hypertension and uremia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
chronic renal failure leads, via a complex mechanism, to a downregulation of Na+/K+ - ATPase and SERCA2a, which in turn produces alterations in calcium cycling and contractility.
chronic renal failure leads, at least in part, to cardiac dysfunction by downregulation of SERCA2a.
chronic renal failure leads, in part, to cardiac dysfunction through a mechanism that involves altered cardiac gene expression, calcium cycling, calcium handling, and contractile function.

renal failure produces a unique pattern of cardiac dysfunction that may be mediated by changes in gene expression.
renal failure leads to changes in calcium cycling and cardiac function.
